subject: Request: short-lived SDK toggle to meet low-latency demo SLA
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 09 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: short-lived SDK toggle to meet low-latency demo SLA

Hi team,

We're scheduled to demo to Nimbus Health next Friday and their evaluation is latency-sensitive — they want 95th pct < 250ms for single-turn scoring calls during our walkthrough. In a few customer demos last month we observed tail latency spikes caused by SDK-side prefix trimming + aggressive reconnects when the connection enrollment is warm. The field asks for a temporary, short-lived SDK toggle we can enable on our hosted route for Nimbus that:  

- disables prefix trimming heuristic (so we avoid extra prefix re-uploads)
- pins connection keepalive to 60s for demo window

Attached are a trimmed trace from yesterday's demo (demo-trace-20280308.txt) and the signed waiver they requested to cover any SLA exceptions on our side.

Questions:  
1) Is exposing a per-customer toggle feasible in the next 5 business days?  
2) What are the telemetry/risk markers we should monitor while this is on?
3) If we can't ship a toggle in time, can platform create a short-lived routing exception to route Nimbus to a dedicated pool configured with pre-warmed connections?

I realize this is an exception request — happy to escalate to product if you need a decision. Need to confirm plan by Tuesday so sales can prepare the runbook for the demo.

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Senior Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: demo-trace-20280308.txt (log), requested-waiver-form.pdf (pdf)

From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 09 Mar 2028 11:01:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: short-lived SDK toggle to meet low-latency demo SLA

Tessa, thanks for the heads-up and for attaching the trace. Quick notes after a first pass:  

- The trace shows frequent reconnects during the demo bursts; that lines up with the SDK reconnect/backoff logic re-establishing KV cache and contributing to tail.
- A per-customer toggle is technically doable, but we need to decide whether it's an SDK-level flag or a serving-route runtime override. SDK flag is faster for upcoming demos if we ship via a quick patch, but that requires a client rollout (we don't control Nimbus's deployed client).
- A routing exception to a pre-warmed Dedicated pool is the lower-risk path and doesn't require changes to external client code. However, capacity usage and cost need Sales/Finance sign-off.

Action items I suggest:  
1) Karthik - can you sanity-check an in-service runtime override that keeps prefix caching sticky + extends keepalive? If that's a simple config flip we can do a route-level toggle.
2) Tessa/Marissa - please confirm whether Nimbus is running our SDK-managed client (ver >= 1.4) or their own integration so we know whether a client-side flag is possible.
3) I'll scope potential platform-side telemetry flags to monitor (connection churn, prefix upload rate, 95th latency per route).

If we can get a runtime override and platform telemetry ready by Tuesday EOD, I think we can avoid a code patch.

- Logan
Principal Product Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Mar 2028 10:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: short-lived SDK toggle to meet low-latency demo SLA

Thanks — I dug into the trace and ran a quick repro on staging. Summary of findings and recommended path:  

Findings:
- The tail spikes are correlated with small bursts that cause the client to re-open connections while server-side cache population is still in progress. The SDK prefix trimming heuristic can trigger a re-send of larger prefixes in some edge cases, which amplifies the window.
- On our side we can avoid most of the penalty by making two runtime options available at the route level:  
  1) keep_prefix_cache_sticky = true  (persist prefix KV across connection churn for N minutes)
  2) keepalive_override_seconds = 60  (override default on the grpc/http proxy layer)

Risk and mitigation:
- keep_prefix_cache_sticky increases memory/time-to-evict for prefix entries. We'll gate it to per-route and add a TTL per-entry to limit accumulation.
- keepalive_override_seconds is low risk; only affects connection longevity and may increase open sockets. We'll limit to a known customer list.

Implementation plan (timeline):
- Today/Tomorrow: implement runtime config knobs behind feature flags (non-breaking). Add telemetry for prefix_upload_rate, connection_reopen_count, route_95pct_latency. (2 engineer-days)
- Wednesday: smoke test on staging with synthetic bursts, runbook for rollback. (1 engineer-day)
- Thursday morning: open the toggle for Nimbus in staging for a dry run.
- Thursday afternoon/Friday morning: enable in prod for the demo window. We'll monitor the three telemetry signals and be prepared to disable.

Operational notes:
- We should require a signed waiver for any SLA deviations (Tessa already has one attached).
- I'll add a short dashboard and an alert pair: 95th latency spike and connection_reopen_count > threshold.

If you sign off I can start the runtime change. Query for Sales: do we want me to update the default eviction TTL for the stickiness from 10m to 5m for demo routes? That reduces accumulation risk but shortens stickiness.

-Karthik
Senior Software Engineer, Runtime

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Alicia Romero <alicia.romero@nimbushealth.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Mar 2028 15:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: short-lived SDK toggle to meet low-latency demo SLA

Thanks Karthik — this plan looks good and conservatively scoped.

Answers:
- Nimbus confirms they use our SDK-managed client v1.4 for the demo (per Marissa). So a client-side patch would be possible but, given timing, the runtime override is preferred.
- Please set TTL to 5m for the demo route; we want to minimize memory impact.

Marissa / Sales: I'll send the signed waiver to legal and confirm billing cost for short-lived dedicated routing if platform decides that's safer. For now, Karthik, please proceed with the runtime knobs behind feature flags and the alerting/dashboards as described. We'll do the staging dry run Thursday and enable Friday for the Nimbus demo.

Alicia — attaching the waiver again and I'll loop in Legal if they have questions. Appreciate the flexibility on timing — we're looking forward to showcasing the low-latency path.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: requested-waiver-form.pdf (pdf)
